_comment: Shared machinery: names no product, no platform, no profile class. Numeric bands are deliberately absent — they express a product's type and spacing scale, so they belong to a profile. A profile may extend this catalog with profile/quality/archetypes.json using the same schema; entries merge by id and the profile wins on collision.

rules._comment: Declared, not measured. Checked before generation starts, from this file alone.
rules._rationale: focus must differ for every pair. commitment needs only two distinct values across the set, so one option may carry its difference on focus alone. Without that slack, a screen whose usable commitment values are {inline, pinned, deferred} has exactly three for exactly three options, and the third comes out contrived.
rules._visualExemption: A 'visual' archetype inherits both axes from the baseline and is exempt. Visual-mode invariants govern it instead.

archetypes.name: Object-first
archetypes.intent: The one thing the user came for is the whole screen; everything else earns its way back in. Reads sparse.
moves: Promote the focal value to the top of the first viewport at display scale.
Merge every supporting label into at most one line beneath it.
Demote all secondary modules below the fold or behind a disclosure.
Make the primary action adjacent to the focal object, not remote from it.
archetypes.avoid: Adding a second element at comparable scale — that is choice-set, not object-first.

archetypes.name: Status-first
archetypes.intent: Where the user stands right now is the headline; the action follows from the status rather than competing with it.
moves: Lead with the current state as a single resolved value, not a label plus a chart.
Put the action directly beneath the status it acts on.
Let secondary facts sit as one quiet supporting line, not their own module.
archetypes.avoid: Two competing status values. Pick the one the user acts on.

archetypes.name: Comparison-first
archetypes.intent: The user is choosing, not confirming; make the options weighable side by side.
moves: Split the single path into peer surfaces that share one comparison dimension.
Align the differing attribute to the same position in every peer so the eye can scan one column.
Give each peer its own action rather than one shared action below.
archetypes.avoid: Peers that differ on more than one dimension at once, leaving no single axis to compare along.

archetypes.name: Guardrail-first
archetypes.intent: What constrains the user is settled before they can act, so the action carries no surprise.
moves: Raise limits, eligibility, and consequences above the primary action in document order.
State each constraint as a resolved value, not a link to go read one.
Let the action stay visually quiet until its preconditions are shown.
archetypes.avoid: Turning constraints into warning styling. Restraint is the point; alarm is a different product.

archetypes.name: Ledger-first
archetypes.intent: The record set is the screen; the user scans and verifies before any single action matters.
moves: Give the repeating row one scannable rhythm and hold every row to it.
Align the value the user compares to the same edge in every row.
Move any summary to a single line above or below the set, never interleaved.
Let each row own its action instead of hoisting one action for the whole set.
archetypes.avoid: Decorating rows until the rhythm breaks. Uniformity is what makes a list scannable.

archetypes.name: Task-first
archetypes.intent: The input the user came to give is the screen; everything else is confirmation of what that input will do.
moves: Put the input at the top of the first viewport, already focused and ready.
Collapse every configurable option into one compact group beneath it.
Keep the commit action reachable without scrolling past the input.
Show the consequence of the current input as one live line, not a separate module.
archetypes.avoid: Explaining the form above the form. Let the field and its one hint carry it.

archetypes.name: Hub-first
archetypes.intent: The screen is a place to leave from; make the destinations legible and equally weighted.
moves: Group destinations by how often they are used, not by internal system category.
Give every destination the same visual weight unless one is genuinely primary.
Keep identity or account context to a single compact header.
Remove any destination the user cannot act on from this state.
archetypes.avoid: A single dominant tile. That is object-first with links attached.

archetypes.name: Quiet / native
archetypes.intent: Recede toward the platform's own defaults; let content carry the hierarchy alone. Reads sparse and flat.
moves: Collapse cards into a single continuous surface separated by the profile's hairline divider.
Remove every radius and shadow not required by an identity anchor.
Let type scale, not enclosure, mark the sections.
archetypes.avoid: Changing what is on the screen. Visual archetypes hold structure and vary treatment.

archetypes.name: Premium / spacious
archetypes.intent: Give the focal content room so it reads as considered rather than crowded.
moves: Increase the space around the focal element more than anywhere else, so the ratio itself creates the hierarchy.
Reduce the number of visible surfaces, merging adjacent ones that carry related content.
Let one generous margin replace two separators.
archetypes.avoid: Uniformly padding everything. That reads as loose, not premium.

archetypes.name: Data-forward
archetypes.intent: Let the numbers, dates and terms set the visual rhythm instead of the containers around them.
moves: Raise the numeric values a step in the type scale and drop their labels a step.
Align numbers on a shared edge so they form a readable column.
Strip container decoration that competes with the values it holds.
archetypes.avoid: Turning the screen into a table. Density is the goal; a grid of borders is not.
